title: session-keyset-leak-and-arena-shear-gpu-oom-hotpatch-rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + dedicated + private) reported sudden GPU OOM cascades during prolonged inference sessions. Investigation showed a formerly low-frequency leak in the session keyset index that pins small persistent allocations inside the GPU arena; over time this prevented slab coalescing and forced the allocator to fragment, culminating in OOMs under normal load. This ticket tracks the triage, reproduction, fix, and staged rollout of a runtime patch and mitigation playbook for customers.
repro_steps: 1) Start long-running multi-turn chat workload with enabled prefix caching and session affinity. 2) Simulate high session churn (create/delete sessions every ~20s). 3) Observe incremental growth of 'pinned_key_bytes' in runtime telemetry and decline in contiguous free GPU arena ranges. 4) Under sustained token throughput (~200-300 tok/s on our test p4d), allocator fails to satisfy large contiguous slab allocation and OOMs.
investigation_notes:
- Initial signs: hosted customer A incident (sev2) on 2026-03-08; dedicated customer B saw repeated restarts and degraded tail latency.
- Telemetry: per-session keyset reference count metric drifted upward for sessions that were marked 'inactive' but not reclaimed.
- Heap snapshots: small persistent keyset descriptors (~1.2KB each) accumulated across thousands of sessions; together they obstructed coalescing of 64MB arena chunks.
- Root cause hypothesis: eviction watermark miscalibration in the session cleaner plus a race in index compaction that left tombstone markers without decrementing the underlying pinned reference.
- Repro verified in lab with a scaled replay harness (see attachments).
hotfix_summary: 1) Preventive guard: add defensive decrement in indexcompactor when tombstone sweep marks entries reclaimed. 2) Immediate mitigation: enable aggressive session scavenger config (reduction of grace window from 5m -> 30s) for impacted clusters. 3) Long-term: introduce compacting copy-path that avoids pinning short-lived descriptors during compaction and a background arena defragmenter task that coalesces free ranges when fragmentation ratio > 0.35.
runbook_actions:
- Immediately applied config change to hosted region us-west-2; observed stabilized free arena ranges within 12 minutes.
- For dedicated/private customers: Ops pushed hotconfig via customer-managed agent with approval.
- Run emergency canary on 10% of nodes in each pool before full rollout.
- Prepare rollback: kernel bump and config revert automated via canary pipeline if OOM rate increases by >= 50% relative to baseline.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: Canary (10% nodes) - 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Stage 2: 50% ramp with monitoring alerts - 2026-03-14 08:00 UTC. Stage 3: global rollout 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Post-rollout verification window: 48h.
Monitoring: GPU OOM count, contiguous-free-arena-metric, session-pinned-keybytes, tail-latency P99.
qa_steps:
- Re-run replay harness for 72h with session churn profile used in customer incidents.
- Confirm pinned_key_bytes remains stable across session churn; fragmentation ratio below 0.25.
- Run randomized failure-injection of compactor to verify defensive decrement does not double-free.
- Run integration tests for on-prem upgrade path (air-gapped) and verify config agent applies correctly.
postmortem_outline: 1) Incident timeline and customer impact (hosts/CDNs affected). 2) Root cause: index compactor race + scavenger tuning drift. 3) Contributing factors: insufficient fragmentation telemetry, missing early warning for pinned small allocations. 4) Corrective actions: patch (PRs linked), new fragmentation SLO, alert on pinned_key_bytes growth, improved canary policy for memory-sensitive commits. 5) Follow-ups (see subtasks).
